title: clearSlip reads a slip across a sentence end
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts clearSlip matched a KNOWN_SLIPS pair or "want" + verb across a sentence end, so "Thank you. Was it good?" became the held fix "Thank you were it good?".

## Description
clearSlip (desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts:205) walks word tokens with the punctuation dropped, so the last word of one sentence and the first of the next read as one pair. The held fix it builds (said = the span, better = the span with the fix) is shown on the recap as English to learn - here a sentence that is wrong. Fixed: a slip stands inside one sentence (no . ! ? between its words; desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts:88). Technique: judgment-guardbands/deterministic-backbone - the code half must be right where it decides alone.

## Flow
- learner says "Thank you. Was it good?" at A2; the tutor returns kind none
- conversation.ts momentOutcome calls clearSlip(reply) (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:340)
- Before: held fix said "Thank you. Was it good?", better "Thank you were it good?", why Say "you were", not "you was"
- After: null; "Thank you. We was happy." still yields "We were happy."

## Expected impact
An A1-A2 learner stops being taught a broken sentence at the end of a scene. Could break: a slip a learner writes with a stray full stop inside it is no longer caught.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no held fix is built from two sentences
Before: 6 of 6 cross-sentence replies gave a held fix (probe, then tools/linga-moment-test.cjs red)
After: 0 of 6; 3 in-sentence rows still found
Method: gate - red-then-green test in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Read every audience list on the folded copy
body:
## Summary
desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts keywordAudience read four of its eight lists on the raw text only, so a l33t spelling of a phrase-list or older-list topic passed as "all".

## Description
keywordAudience (desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts:74) folded the text (diacritics off, l33t mapped back) and read NEVER, NEVER_MORE, ADULT, ADULT_MORE on both copies, but ADULT_PHRASES, BAR, OLDER, OLDER_PHRASES on the raw text only. "a second d4te", "we place b3ts", "meet at the b4r" read "all" (plain: "adult"); "a j0b interview", "argu3 with my boss" read "all" (plain: "older"). Every list now reads both copies. Technique: prompt-safety/output-sanitization - normalize encodings first, then match every rule on the normalized form.

## Flow
- a pitch or partner line says "a second d4te"
- audienceOf / partnerLine call keywordAudience
- Before: "all" - shown to a child profile
- After: "adult" - refused / redirected as the plain spelling is

## Expected impact
Family-mode learners no longer receive l33t-spelled adult or older topics the plain spelling would stop. Could break: an over-block on a word that folds into a listed one (the gate only narrows; benign rows pinned).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a l33t spelling is never laxer than the plain one
Before: 5 of 7 l33t pairs read laxer (new test in tools/adult-rules-test.cjs red)
After: 0 of 7; 3 benign rows stay "all"
Method: gate - red-then-green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
keywordAudience('a second d4te') 'all' vs keywordAudience('a second date') 'adult'
keywordAudience('a j0b interview') 'all' vs 'older'
desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts:74 (before: OLDER.test(text) || OLDER_PHRASES.test(text) on text only)

title: keepsTense reads the one irregular-past list
body:
## Summary
plain.ts keepsTense knew 17 irregular pasts while gate.ts knew 46, so a beginner's present coached into an irregular past ("I sleep" -> "I slept") passed the plain-coaching rule.

## Description
Two implementations of "is this a past form": desk/src/lib/english/plain.ts (17 forms) and desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts:140 PAST_IRREGULAR (46). keepsTense guards momentOutcome (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:332) and the coach (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:777) for A1-A2; with slept/swam/felt/thought/met/wrote/drank/taught unknown, the present->past fix reached the beginner. gate.ts now exports the list; plain.ts reads it (plus did/was/were/had) less "left"/"lost" (desk/src/lib/english/plain.ts:25). Registry law: one-authority-per-vocabulary.

## Flow
- an A2 learner says "I sleep well"; the model fixes it to "I slept well"
- momentOutcome: keepsTense(said, better)
- Before: true - the moment stands
- After: false - the moment is dropped as the PLAIN rule intends

## Expected impact
Beginners stop being pushed into a past tense they did not use. Could break: a better that uses one of the 29 newly read forms in a non-past sense is dropped (left and lost excluded for that reason).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one list decides past forms for both rules
Before: 7 of 8 present->past rows passed keepsTense; lists 17 vs 46
After: 0 of 8; 4 tense-keeping rows stay true; one list
Method: gate - red-then-green in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
keepsTense('I sleep well','I slept well') true (before)
plain.ts IRREGULAR: did|was|were|had|went|ate|saw|made|took|came|got|bought|gave|knew|told|found|said (17)
gate.ts PAST_IRREGULAR: 46 forms

title: "to" and "ten" no longer read as Czech in easing
body:
## Summary
ease.ts CZECH_WORDS held the English words "to" and "ten", so a short English answer ("Ten.", "To school") read as Czech and eased the partner.

## Description
mostlyCzech (desk/src/lib/english/ease.ts) counts a reply Czech when half its words are on CZECH_WORDS (desk/src/lib/english/ease.ts:11). With "to" and "ten" on it, the one- and two-word answers beginners give most read as having left English; learnerLost fired and the turn carried EASE_INSTRUCTION (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:162). Both removed; Czech replies still read Czech on their other words.

## Flow
- partner asks "How many minutes?"; learner answers "Ten minutes."
- learnerLost -> mostlyCzech
- Before: true - next partner line forced to a one-word question
- After: false

## Expected impact
A beginner who answered is no longer talked down to on the next line. Could break: a Czech reply made only of "to"/"ten" plus English words no longer eases.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - short English answers are English
Before: 4 of 5 short English answers eased (probe; test red)
After: 0 of 5; 5 of 5 Czech rows still Czech
Method: gate - red-then-green in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: learnerLost([{text:'Ten'}]) true; ('Ten minutes.') true; ('To school') true (before)

title: A "what" inside the learner's own question is not lost
body:
## Summary
ease.ts saysLost matched the bare word "what" anywhere, so every learner question with "what" ("What do you sell?") read as not understanding and eased the partner.

## Description
NOT_UNDERSTOOD (desk/src/lib/english/ease.ts:13) ended in a bare "what" alternative, matched as a whole word anywhere. Asking questions is a scene skill; each such question triggered EASE_INSTRUCTION. Now "what" counts lost alone or with sorry/pardon, and "What do you mean?" / "What does that mean?" stay lost (desk/src/lib/english/ease.ts:26).

## Flow
- learner in a shop scene asks "What do you sell?"
- learnerLost -> saysLost
- Before: true - partner told to ask one short question with no new vocabulary
- After: false; "What?" and "Sorry, what?" still true

## Expected impact
Learners who ask questions keep a partner at their level. Could break: a lost learner who says "What is that?" no longer eases.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - only not-understanding eases
Before: 5 of 5 learner questions with "what" eased
After: 0 of 5; 9 of 9 not-understood rows still lost
Method: gate - red on a scratch copy of the test (suite could not load: another agent mid-edit in check.ts), green in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
saysLost('What do you sell?') true; saysLost('What time is it?') true (before)
tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:3390 keeps 'What?' eased

title: Key the phone door's answer table by the actions the phone posts
body:
## Summary
phoneDoor.ts ANSWERS was a hand-written Record<string,...> with nothing tying it to the commands the phone posts; a missing entry is a runtime 409 with every gate green.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/phoneDoor.ts:24 maps each phone command to the hand-off kind that answers it. Its ground truth is lingaView's Answer["action"] and wordsJob's WordsJob (desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:127, desk/src/lib/english/view.ts:285) plus preferences. Typed as Record<Answer["action"] | WordsJob | "preferences", ...>, a new answer action or words job missing from the table fails tsc. Method 4.7 (hand-maintained list).

## Flow
- seed: delete "moment-try" from ANSWERS
- Before: tsc exit 0 - the phone's try would be refused "The TV is not asking for that now."
- After: tsc exit 2, TS2741 "moment-try" missing

## Expected impact
A future Linga answer action cannot ship refused at the door. Could break: nothing at runtime (lookup unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the table derives from its ground truth
Before: seeded drift -> tsc exit 0
After: seeded drift -> tsc exit 2; unseeded exit 0
Method: gate - tsc on a seeded violation, both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
const ANSWERS: Record<string, "reply" | "words" | "prefs"> (before)
seeded tsc: src/lib/english/phoneDoor.ts(24,7): error TS2741: Property '"moment-try"' is missing

title: A gym bag, a PE bag or a lunch bag says no place
body:
## Summary
lostfound.ts readReply read "gym bag", "PE bag" and "lunch bag" as a bag plus a place, narrowing the lost-property table on a place nobody said.

## Description
VOCAB (desk/src/lib/english/lostfound.ts:122) reads two-word phrases first but had none for these compounds, so "gym"/"pe" (gym) and "lunch" (canteen) were read as places. A learner naming the kind of bag put aside things that matched and could put their own bag aside. Added as two-word kind phrases.

## Flow
- learner: "My gym bag." in the lost jacket scene
- settle -> readReply
- Before: is {kind:bag, place:gym}
- After: is {kind:bag}; "I left my bag in the gym" still reads place gym

## Expected impact
The table moves only on what was said. Could break: a learner meaning "the bag from the gym" by "gym bag" no longer narrows by place.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - descriptions narrow on what was said
Before: 4 of 4 compound-bag replies carried a place
After: 0 of 4
Method: gate - red-then-green in tools/linga-lost-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none

title: slipStands and findKey keep a key inside one sentence
body:
## Summary
The pair of the clearSlip fix: slipStands and findKey, the key-match helpers every slip and find judge uses, still matched a key across a sentence end.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts:146 findKey and desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts:164 slipStands match word tokens with punctuation dropped. "Thank you. Was it good?" stood as the slip "you was"; review.ts slipsAgain/markSlipped (desk/src/lib/english/review.ts:272, desk/src/lib/english/review.ts:289) can count it a slip again (a fossil stop, a record write), and lineFound / judgeTry / usesFrame can find a key across two sentences. One helper (desk/src/lib/english/slip.ts:88) now holds findKey, slipStands and clearSlip.

## Flow
- learner who was taught "you was" -> "you were" says "Thank you. Was it good?"
- slipsAgain -> slipIn -> slipStands
- Before: "you. Was" - the slip stands again
- After: null

## Expected impact
No slip or find is counted from two sentences. Could break: an abbreviation with a full stop inside a key ("Mr. Smith") no longer matches.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - slips and finds stand inside one sentence
Before: 5 of 5 cross-sentence rows matched by both helpers
After: 0 of 5; in-sentence and decimal rows unchanged; 19 lib/english suites green
Method: gate - red-then-green in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
slipStands('Thank you. Was it good?','you was') -> 'you. Was'
slipStands('My tomatoes. Is it big?','tomatoes is') -> 'tomatoes. Is'
findKey same rows non-null (before)

title: The duet caption no longer sends the co-star to a phone helper
body:
## Summary
duet.ts beatCaption told the room "Mum can open the co-star helper there" (on the phone), a control TL-12 removed from the phone; the file header made the same claim.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/duet.ts:165 beatCaption (the TV caption slot on the learner's beat) and the header at desk/src/lib/english/duet.ts:11 described a phone helper; tools/linga-duet-test.cjs:246 pins that the phone holds none - the helper is the TV's cue action ("Help me answer"). Caption now: "Mum can ask the TV for help." (label-neutral: the action reads "More help" after one rung); header names the cue action.

## Flow
- duet scene, learner's beat
- TV caption via lingaView -> beatCaption
- Before: "... Mum can open the co-star helper there."
- After: "... Mum can ask the TV for help."

## Expected impact
The co-star looks where the help is. Could break: nothing; owed: a Playwright capture of the caption.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the caption names a control that exists
Before: 1 of 1 learner's-beat captions named a phone helper; 2 sentences asserting it
After: 0 and 0
Method: gate - red-then-green in tools/linga-duet-test.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
duet.ts (before): text: `${me} answers first on the phone. ${d.coStar} can open the co-star helper there.`
tools/linga-duet-test.cjs:246 assert.doesNotMatch(sf.phone,/Co-star helper/,'the phone holds no helper (TL-12)')

title: Request credit counts "like", "can" and "may" statements as requests
instrument: Run creditOf(quote,"request",shown,own) over every request-tagged observation in uat/runs (the LT corpus) under A (today's REQUEST_MARKERS) and B (markers as phrases: "would like", "'d like", "can i", "can you", "could", "may i", "please", "need", "want", or "?"); count the quotes that flip own->none and have the owner read the flipped rows. Pin B with a creditOf table in tools/linga-credit-test.cjs.
body:
## Summary
credit.ts shaped() credits a "request" quote as own when it holds any of can/could/would/please/need/want/like/may, so plain statements ("I like dogs", "I can swim") earn request credit when the model tags them.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/credit.ts:11 REQUEST_MARKERS are single words; desk/src/lib/english/credit.ts:48 accepts any of them. "like" and "can"/"may" are request markers only in frames ("I would like", "Can I", "May I"). Code is the backbone that bounds the model's skill tag (judgment-guardbands/deterministic-backbone); here the bound is wide enough that a mis-tag earns evidence. Fixed would be phrase-level markers.

## Flow
- the tutor tags "I like dogs" as request, success
- validateObservations -> creditOf(quote,"request")
- Today: own - evidence written to the learner record
- Proposed: none; "I would like a coffee" and "Can I have water?" stay own

## Expected impact
The request skill on the learner record reflects requests. Could break: genuine requests phrased with a bare marker lose credit - the corpus run measures how many. credit.ts is on the live surface: a drift record is owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only request-shaped quotes earn request credit
Before: 3 of 3 non-request statements ("I like dogs", "I can swim", "I may go home later") credited own
After: not built - the corpus run decides how many real requests B would lose
Method: probe - creditOf on 6 quotes; the corpus experiment needs uat/runs and an owner read
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
creditOf('I like dogs','request',[]) -> 'own'
creditOf('I can swim','request',[]) -> 'own'
creditOf('I may go home later','request',[]) -> 'own'
desk/src/lib/english/credit.ts:11

title: Merge gate.ts ADULT_PHRASES into the ADULT list it mostly repeats
instrument: Generate the union of every alternative in ADULT, ADULT_PHRASES and ADULT_MORE with each English ending plus the ROWS table in tools/adult-rules-test.cjs and the l33t pairs; run keywordAudience on A and on B (one ADULT list with second/third/next/romantic dates and bets folded in, ADULT_PHRASES deleted); B lands only with 0 rows differing.
body:
## Summary
gate.ts keeps the "first backstop" ADULT_PHRASES whole beside the ADULT word list; 19 of its 21 alternatives repeat ADULT, so the adult vocabulary has two hand-maintained copies.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts:28 ADULT and desk/src/lib/english/gate.ts:49 ADULT_PHRASES overlap on dating, romance, romantic, flirt, boyfriend, girlfriend, kiss, alcohol, beer, wine, drunk, drug, gambl, casino, betting, sex, sexual, first/blind date, on/for a date, date night; only second/third/next/romantic date(s) and bets are unique to ADULT_PHRASES. The parity fix (da6a7418) had to remember both copies; a widening written into one list is the drift one-authority-per-vocabulary forbids. The comment keeps the second list "so the merged gate is at least as strict as either" - an equivalence a test can prove instead.

## Flow
- fold the 2 unique alternatives into ADULT
- delete ADULT_PHRASES and its two read sites
- run the equivalence corpus on both sides; 0 differences

## Expected impact
One list for a teacher to read before a release ("A PERSON MUST READ THESE LISTS"). Could break: a missed alternative loosens the safety gate - hence the corpus gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authoritative adult list
Before: 21 ADULT_PHRASES alternatives, 19 duplicated in ADULT (counted)
After: 0 duplicates, proven equivalent by corpus - not built
Method: probe - counted the overlap by hand; equivalence needs the corpus run
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Four server-memory maps hold hidden halves with one copied idiom and no loss trace
instrument: Build a boundedMemory(name, cap) helper in lib/english with a lost-on-read counter exposed to a rules test; migrate help.ts, line.ts, lostfound.ts and repair.ts; test: 4 sites -> 1, and a simulated restart (clear the globalThis maps) mid-scene shows the counter at 1 for each of the line, lost and repair reads.
body:
## Summary
help.ts, line.ts, lostfound.ts and repair.ts each keep a hidden half (ladder, line, lost target, withheld fix) in a globalThis Map with the same hand-copied insertion-order cap, and a restart that loses one leaves no record.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/line.ts:61, desk/src/lib/english/lostfound.ts:242, desk/src/lib/english/repair.ts:54 and desk/src/lib/english/help.ts:139 repeat `while (m.size > CAP) m.delete(m.keys().next().value!)` with caps 200/100/200/200. Each degrades on a restart by design (no line, the task stands down, the moment marks itself lost) but nothing counts it, so a desk restart that cost a learner the scene's line or a withheld fix is invisible to the operator. Out of scope for one file: help.ts is in the linga context.

## Flow
- desk restarts mid-scene
- heldLine / lostTurn / revealed return null
- Today: the scene falls back silently
- Proposed: one helper, one counter a test and the operator can read

## Expected impact
The operator can tell how often a restart cost a learner a hidden line or fix. Could break: eviction order if the helper changed it (keep insertion order).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - 4 duplicated sites to 1, loss counted
Before: 4 sites, 0 loss counters (grep)
After: 1 helper, 1 counter - not built
Method: probe - grep of the idiom across lib/english
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep keys().next().value desk/src/lib/english: help.ts:139, line.ts:61, lostfound.ts:242, repair.ts:54

title: The replay frame misses a contracted form said in full ("does not" for "doesn't")
instrument: A usesFrame table in tools/linga-moment-test.cjs: the 5 probe rows (doesn't/does not, can't/can not, won't/will not, isn't/is not, cannot/can't) plus the existing replay rows; B normalises contractions to their full words in replay.ts tokens (both frame and reply) and must keep every existing frameOf/invitesFrame/replayRefused row green.
body:
## Summary
replay.ts norm folds only "can't" to "cannot", so a learner who says the coached negative in full ("He does not like fish" for "He doesn't like it") is judged not to use the frame.

## Description
desk/src/lib/english/replay.ts:29 maps one spelling; frameOf (desk/src/lib/english/replay.ts:41) keeps "doesn't", "won't", "isn't" as single tokens and usesFrame (desk/src/lib/english/replay.ts:62) compares word for word. "can not" (two words) misses "cannot" too. conversation.ts reads usesFrame to say whether the Back replay used the coached form (desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:220), so a correct use goes uncounted. Two spellings of one form, only one normalised.

## Flow
- moment: "He not like it" -> "He doesn't like it"; Back replay asks about food
- learner: "He does not like fish"
- Today: usesFrame null - the replay counts as not used
- Proposed: "He does not like" matches the frame

## Expected impact
Learners who use the full form get the credit for it. Could break: anchors and invitesFrame change with multi-word frames - the table gate holds them.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a coached form is recognised in either spelling
Before: 4 of 5 contraction variants missed (probe)
After: not built
Method: probe - frameOf/usesFrame on 5 rows
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
usesFrame('He does not like fish', frameOf({kind:'fix',said:'He not like it',better:"He doesn't like it"})) -> null
usesFrame('I can not swim', frame of "I can't swim") -> null
usesFrame('I will not go', frame of "I won't go") -> null
usesFrame('She is not here', frame of "She isn't here") -> null
